reasoning_content:
The command exits RC=0 quickly. Wait, "tail -f /dev/null" should keep it running. But it returned immediately. The issue: the `&` after Xvfb backgrounds... let's trace: 

The command is `sh -c "... && Xvfb ... & sleep 2 && grep ... && nginx && spawn-fcgi ... && tail -f /dev/null"`. 

Actually the tricky part: the `&` at the end of the Xvfb line backgrounds the entire compound command up to that point! In shell, `A && B && C &` backgrounds the whole list `A && B && C`. So the command `mkdir ... && cat ... && ... && Xvfb ...` runs in background, and then `sleep 2 && grep && nginx && spawn-fcgi && tail -f /dev/null` runs in foreground. Hmm, that would still keep tail -f running.

Wait actually in POSIX shell, `&` has lower precedence than `&&`. So `cmd1 && cmd2 & cmd3` means `(cmd1 && cmd2) &` then `cmd3`. So the first group is backgrounded.

But the redeeming: when run via `sh -c 'sh /cmd.sh'`, the outer process exits when inner finishes. The inner had `tail -f /dev/null` at the end. Hmm but RC=0 returned immediately, meaning tail didn't block. 

Hmm wait, maybe the heredoc consumed the rest of the script? Look at the command: 
```
cat > /etc/postgresql-common/pg_service.conf <<EOF
[qonnectra] host=... EOF
  mkdir -p ...
```
The heredoc terminator is `EOF` and it appears on the same line as content: `[qonnectra] host=... EOF`. Actually the heredoc content is everything until a line containing just `EOF`. Here the line is `[qonnectra] host=db port=5432 dbname=qonnectra user=qgis_user password=local_dev_qgis_password_123 sslmode=disable EOF` — this line does NOT equal `EOF`, so the heredoc continues consuming subsequent lines until it finds a line that is exactly `EOF`. There is no such line! So the heredoc consumes the ENTIRE rest of the script including `tail -f /dev/null`.

That means the `cat >` writes all the remaining lines to pg_service.conf, and there's nothing left to execute → script ends with RC=0. That's why the container exits immediately with code 0 → restart loop.

This is a real bug in docker-compose.dev.yml: the heredoc `<<EOF` ... `EOF` format is broken because the `EOF` is on the same line as the content. Actually wait — in the YAML the `>` folded block, lines get joined by spaces. So the heredoc end delimiter `EOF` ends up placed at the end of the content line, not on its own line. That breaks the heredoc.

In docker-compose.yml (production), they used the `printf` approach which works. So the dev compose is genuinely buggy.

So the dev compose has at least 2 bugs:
1. nginx: `./nginx/nginx.conf` mounted to `/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf` — wrong. Should be nginx.conf → /etc/nginx/nginx.conf and default.conf → /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf.
2. qgis-server: broken heredoc causing immediate exit.

Also the tileserver needs germany.mbtiles which isn't in the repo (documented as user-generated). So tileserver will restart.

Given the guide says `docker-compose up -d --build` from deployment (production compose) is the Quick Start. The dev compose is method 2. Let me try the production compose instead, which may avoid the dev bugs. But production uses Caddyfile.production with Let's Encrypt — for .localhost domains Caddy will use internal CA (localhost domains are served with internal CA automatically). Actually Caddy auto-issues for localhost with internal CA. Fine.

But production compose also doesn't have the frontend env_file? It has env_file: .env. That works.

Yes, this mounts the full nginx.conf (which has `http {}`, `events {}`) into conf.d/default.conf → nginx errors "worker_processes directive is not allowed here". This is a clear bug. Production has both mounts correct.

So dev compose is broken for nginx. And the qgis heredoc is broken. Both are real repo bugs.
